Legal Precedents Mentioned:

1. Smith v. Maryland
2. Jones v. United States

Similarities to the Case at Hand:
The text indicates that the principle established in Smith v. Maryland, known as the third-party doctrine, was applied in Jones v. United States. Specifically, the court in Jones referenced Smith to support the ruling that an individual does not have a reasonable expectation of privacy for information voluntarily shared with third parties.
